html:
A Celtic people who lived both in central Europe and in northern Italy. The map shows them in 500 and 400 BCE in Emilia, around modern Bologna.

The Boii crossed the Alps around 400 BCE, part of the great Celtic movement into Italy that also brought the sack of Rome. They took the Etruscan city of Felsina and made it their centre. For two centuries they fought Rome, often alongside other Gauls. Rome beat a large Gallic army that included them at Telamon in 225 BCE, they backed Hannibal in the Second Punic War, and in 191 BCE Rome finally conquered them. Felsina became the Roman colony of Bononia.

Other Boii lived north of the Alps, and their name survives in Bohemia, land of the Boii. These northern Boii were beaten by the Dacians under Burebista in the 1st century BCE. All belonged to the La Tène Celtic world, and their neighbours in Italy were the Etruscans.
sum: A Celtic people who lived both in central Europe and in northern Italy. The map shows them in 500 and 400 BCE in Emilia, around modern Bologna.
